The Squeeze Theorem

A sequence trapped between two others takes the stage. When both sides head to the same value, the middle follows.

The middle sequence never needs measuring directly. If both guards walk through the same door, whatever stands between them goes through it as well. Oscillating sequences are caught this way too: ∣sin⁡n∣≤1|\sin n| \le 1∣sinn∣≤1 traps sin⁡nn\frac{\sin n}{n}nsinn​ between ±1n\pm\frac{1}{n}±n1​, and since both sides tend to 0, so does the middle.

For example, picture a 🧍 person walking down a corridor. If both walls narrow in to a single point, the person, unable to pass through walls, must end up at that same point.

Using the squeeze theorem, prove completely that lim⁡n→∞sin⁡nn=0\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\sin n}{n} = 0limn→∞​nsinn​=0.

−1n≤sin⁡nn≤1n-\frac{1}{n} \le \frac{\sin n}{n} \le \frac{1}{n}−n1​≤nsinn​≤n1​
Show proof

  1. For every real ttt, ∣sin⁡t∣≤1|\sin t| \le 1∣sint∣≤1. Dividing by n≥1n \ge 1n≥1 gives −1n≤sin⁡nn≤1n-\frac{1}{n} \le \frac{\sin n}{n} \le \frac{1}{n}−n1​≤nsinn​≤n1​.

  2. Both ends tend to 0: 1n→0\frac{1}{n} \to 0n1​→0 and −1n→0-\frac{1}{n} \to 0−n1​→0 (the Archimedean corollary). The squeeze theorem now gives sin⁡nn→0\frac{\sin n}{n} \to 0nsinn​→0.

Using the squeeze theorem, prove completely that lim⁡n→∞n+(−1)nn=1\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{n + (-1)^n}{n} = 1limn→∞​nn+(−1)n​=1.

n−1n≤n+(−1)nn≤n+1n\frac{n - 1}{n} \le \frac{n + (-1)^n}{n} \le \frac{n + 1}{n}nn−1​≤nn+(−1)n​≤nn+1​
Show proof

  1. Since (−1)n(-1)^n(−1)n is either −1-1−1 or 111, −1≤(−1)n≤1-1 \le (-1)^n \le 1−1≤(−1)n≤1. Adding nnn and dividing by nnn gives n−1n≤n+(−1)nn≤n+1n\frac{n - 1}{n} \le \frac{n + (-1)^n}{n} \le \frac{n + 1}{n}nn−1​≤nn+(−1)n​≤nn+1​.

  2. The left end is n−1n=1−1n→1\frac{n - 1}{n} = 1 - \frac{1}{n} \to 1nn−1​=1−n1​→1 and the right end is n+1n=1+1n→1\frac{n + 1}{n} = 1 + \frac{1}{n} \to 1nn+1​=1+n1​→1. By the squeeze theorem the middle tends to 1 as well.
